rule.name: FutureJoinedWhereStarted
rule.message: A future is started and waited for in the same step, so the tasks run one at a time. In a stream, map(id -> supplyAsync(...)) followed by map(CompletableFuture::join) moves one element through every stage before it takes the next: it starts one task, waits for it, and only then starts the next, with a thread hop added. The same holds for supplyAsync(...).join() or runAsync(...).join() written as one expression. Start all the tasks first and join afterwards: collect the futures into a list (toList()), then pending.stream().map(CompletableFuture::join).toList(). If the work is not meant to run concurrently, call the method directly. An exception fits a single call that is moved to another executor on purpose.
